eli (docs): Hey folks — opening a PR to refresh the model catalog entries and per-model cards. Primary goals: clarify supported context vs runtime-accepted window, add quantized variant rows, include small SDK examples, and fix a few broken links. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4897

tess (ml): Nice. I can provide vetted numbers for the q4_* and q5_1 variants. Quick summary for the card:
- mistral-7b (float): trained 32k, runtime-accepted 32k, best perf on a100-80gb ~6.1 tok/ms (batch=1), p4d-8x ~5.9 tok/ms.
- mistral-7b-q4_0: runtime-accepted 32k, ~9.5 tok/ms on p4d-8x.
- llama3-8b: trained 16k, runtime accepts up to 32k (soft-truncate after 20k). Mark runtime-supported = 32k with degrade note.

omar (infra): @eli note for Private/Dedicated customers: older control planes (pre-2024-10) may not load q5 artifacts cleanly. Recommend doc snippet for upgrade: 

```
# upgrade control-plane and agents
rwctl upgrade control-plane --image=redwood/control-plane:v2024.10.3
rwctl agents upgrade --image=redwood/runtime:rwinf-2025.01
```

Also add: per-shard KV cache limit = 48GB (Dedicated nodes). Rolling upgrades preserve sessions but require KV cache flush for model shard swaps.

eli (docs): Thanks — I'll add that migration code block in the migration section.

riley (product): Editorial: please add a short "who should use this variant" line. E.g., "mistral-7b-q4_0 — recommended for low-latency, cost-sensitive text generation; not recommended for numeric-exact tasks". Also keep marketing-friendly rounded benchmarks on the card and hide raw CSV in expandable.

tess (ml): I've uploaded raw benchmark CSVs to the bucket: s3://redwood-bench/mistral-7b/quant/runs/2025-03-01.csv. Will link from the PR comment.

eli (docs): Can someone paste a minimal Python SDK example and a curl example I can include? Need both streaming and non-streaming variants.

tess (ml): Python non-streaming:

```
from redwood import RedwoodClient
rc = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_KEY'))
resp = rc.generate(model='mistral-7b-q4_0', input='Explain zero-shot prompting', max_tokens=120)
print(resp.text)
```

Python streaming:

```
for chunk in rc.stream_generate(model='mistral-7b-q4_0', input='Write a short poem', max_tokens=64):
    print(chunk.text, end='')
```

Curl example:

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"mistral-7b-q4_0","input":"Hello","max_tokens":32}'
```

eli (docs): Great — I'll paste those in. Also adding a short test under docs/examples/smoke/ that runs the non-streaming snippet and asserts it returns text.

docs-ci: [auto] link-check: discovered one broken link in llama3 card (old vendor page). Flagged.

omar (infra): Small caveat to document: when we route to a quantized variant we sometimes fall back to a float variant for long sequences if quantized artifact has lower KV cache headroom. Add a "fallback behavior" line under compatibility.

eli (docs): Good — we'll add a small compatibility table: Hosted / Dedicated / Private row with notes about runtime versions and KV limits. Also adding a Known Issues entry for q5_1 (lab-tested, higher latency variance on small GPUs).

tess (ml): One more: mark which variants are compatible with Redwood Optimize auto-quantize suggestions (q4_0 and q5_1 flagged as eligible; q5_1 experimental).

eli (docs): Copy. I'll also normalize model names to canonical IDs in the catalog (lowercase, hyphenated) and mention internal artifact tags in parentheses.

riley (product): Quick ask — can we avoid publishing raw per-run token/sec in the summary rows? Keep high-level rounded values and exacts in the CSV. Marketing will be happier. :+1:

eli (docs): Will do. Plan to merge after CI passes and after @tess and @omar sign off on infra notes. Targeting merge in ~1hr. Tag me in PR if you see anything.

docs-ci: [auto] checklist: metadata present, sdk-snippets present, migration guide present, benchmarks linked, example tests missing.

eli (docs): I'll push the smoke test now and ping. Thanks everyone! :rocket:
